A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

single photon detection in superconducting nanoscale structures could be realized if the strip is relatively clean (small $D$), the strip is thin (small $d$) and the photon is absorbed at the center of the strip.

The main takeaway from our work is that
superconducting nanosized structures with $C_e / C_{ph} \sim 10-100$ at temperatures below $T_c$ could be good candidates for single photon detection.
superconducting single-photon detectors should have $C_e/C_ph|_{T_c} > 1$ to be effective.
